svg.text: Footswitch box — wiring layout (matches YOUR wiring view)

Mirrored left-right from the drill-template/top-view coordinates in pipedal-hardware-v2.md — confirmed against your own row-by-row description: TUNER/MUTE + USB coupler on the left, RESET on the right, Pico on the right wall. Wire paths are simplified straight lines, not exact dressed routing.
(moved here — left of OLED, more room)
ribbon, plug-in — header edge should face
RIGHT (toward Pico) — dress the ribbon clear of
the encoder's knob, which now sits in that path →
Signal wire — soldered at the part, plug-in (Dupont socket) at the Pico header
Ground wire — soldered at the part, joins the ground bus
LED anode wire (through its resistor) — soldered, plug-in at the Pico
Plug-in only, no solder anywhere (OLED ribbon, both USB cables)
Ground bus — twist-and-solder joint, or a screw terminal strip
Mechanical fastening only, no wire — nut/bolt/screw (switch bushings,
OLED mounting screws, USB coupler bolts, encoder bushing)
Friction-fit + optional dab of glue (LED body in its panel hole)
Taped down — double-sided mounting tape over an insulation layer
(Pico only, on the RIGHT WALL — a fixed wall, not the removable access lid)
L1/L2 = the switch's 2 used lugs (of 6 — it's a DPDT, only one pole's COM+NO pair is wired). L1 = signal (red), L2 = ground (black).
Encoder: A/B = quadrature signal, C = their shared ground, SW1 = push-switch signal, SW2 = push-switch ground.
Full pin table: pipedal-footswitch-wiring-reference.md. Build order: pipedal-footswitch-wiring-procedure.md.
Pico is on a FIXED wall (not the detachable access lid) — every switch/OLED/encoder is on the fixed ceiling too, so nothing here ever needs to disconnect when the box is opened.
Identifying your 2 lugs (this switch is a DPDT — 6 lugs, only 2 used)
Confirmed: one face of the base is stamped "M 1 2 3" — M is the body-length code (matches the -M
in SF12N-0202-20R-M), 1/2/3 are the real pin numbers. Wire lugs 1 and 2 (marked), leave 3 unconnected.
Wire the marked pins, verify with a multimeter first:
1. Find the face stamped "M 1 2 3" — wire lugs 1 and 2. Leave 3
unconnected, and the entire opposite face untouched.
2. Quick check before soldering (continuity mode, switch
unpressed): lugs 1+2 should read open, then closed while you
hold the switch pressed. Confirms you're reading the right
face before solder goes on — costs 5 seconds.
No marking, or can't read it? Fall back to multimeter alone:
3. Try lug pairs until one goes open→closed exactly as above.
That's your pair — 3rd lug of that group + whole other pole
stay unconnected, same as the marked case.
Do this per switch — don't assume all ten seat/read the same way.
OLED wiring detail — 7 pins, fully plug-in, no soldering
Pin order along the header below is illustrative/generic, NOT confirmed for your specific module. Read the label
PRINTED on your board's silkscreen next to each pin and match it to the Pico target here — go by name, not position.
the right wall (Pico), away from encoder
The one connection that can damage the display: VCC must land on 3V3(OUT), never VBUS/5V.
Every other pin, if swapped, just gives a blank/garbled screen — no solder to undo, just re-check
and re-plug the ribbon. It's a single female-female Dupont ribbon (7 of 10 conductors used),
plugging straight onto both the OLED's header and the Pico's — no cutting, no soldering at all.
Full pin table + reasoning: pipedal-footswitch-wiring-reference.md, "OLED" section.
CONFIRMED, both from the datasheet AND multimeter-tested on your actual part. Datasheet's front
view (knob facing you) reads bottom 3 pins A-C-B left to right — but that's the OPPOSITE face from
where you're wiring. Mirrored for YOUR view from below: bottom reads B-C-A left to right (below).
Top 2 = SW1/SW2, confirmed by your own multimeter test (open at rest, closed only when pressed).
quadrature — turning the shaft (bottom, YOUR view from below)
Pico target — all 5 soldered at encoder,
C → ground bus (shared return for A/B)
SW2 → ground bus (push switch's own return)
only SW1 shares the same debounce logic
C and SW2 are two separate lugs on the part —
both end up on the same ground bus, but they're
not internally the same pin, wire both.
Distance to Pico: ~90-110mm (300mm jumper, plenty of slack).
